South Africa, officially the Republic of South Africa (RSA), is the southernmost country in Africa. It has nine provinces bounded by the South Atlantic and Indian Oceans to the south, and neighboring countries including Namibia, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Mozambique, Eswatini, and it encloses Lesotho. Its population is over 63 million, making it the 6th largest in Africa. The administrative capital is Pretoria, legislative capital is Cape Town, and judicial capital is Bloemfontein. Johannesburg is the largest city.

The country has a rich history, with indigenous Khoisan people and Bantu-speaking peoples, colonization by the Dutch and British, and apartheid until 1994. It’s known as the "rainbow nation" for its cultural diversity. South Africa has the largest economy in Africa and is a middle power internationally. It faces challenges like crime, poverty, and inequality.

when did it become a republic

South Africa became a republic on 31 May 1961 following a referendum (only white voters participated) that narrowly passed in favor of becoming a republic. Before that, it was the Union of South Africa under the British Crown.
